findings.title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
findings.comment: Observed that unwrapped drinking straws were made available to customers in the bar area to grab with barehands. CORRECTED: PIC and staff were educated that this exposes the food-contact surfaces of the straws to barehand contact by everyone, and that unwrapped straws should be removed from the customer area and only handled with gloved hands by staff (with the gloves acting as a barrier) or the unwrapped straws should be replaced with wrapped straws, where the wrapping acts as a barrier preventing barehand contact. Staff moved the unwrapped straws behind the bar area out of reach of customers, and the PIC plans to purchase wrapped straws instead. Ensure food-contact surfaces of straws are handled with a barrier to prevent barehand contact.
findings.citation_text: 3-301.11(B) Preventing Contamination from Hands. (B) Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in (D) and (E) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact exposed, READY-TO-EAT FOOD with their bare hands and shall use suitable UTENSILS such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing EQUIPMENT. [P]

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: Observed that the handwashing sink in the bar area had a strainer inside of it, obstructing the sink from being used for handwashing and and the handwashing sink was being used for purposes other than handwashing. CORRECTED: the strainer was removed and staff was reminded that handwashing sinks must only be used for handwashing purposes, nothing else. Ensure that handwashing sinks are accessible and maintained at all times for handwashing use by employees, and only for handwashing.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions. [Pf]

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment:
Observed comminuted ground meat (burgers) stored over whole fish and frog legs (which are included in the “FISH” category by the FDA) in the walk-in cooler. CORRECTED: PIC moved the fish and frog legs to a different shelf where they were not below meat of a higher final cooking temperature. Ensure that storage order in coolers are in order of final cooking temperature, so that any cross-contamination from above is resolved with the higher cooking temperature of the item below.
- Top shelf = ready-to-eat food (RTE) which does not require cooking;
- 2nd shelf = fresh unprepared produce that requires washing or cooking
- 3rd shelf = whole meats (fish and frog legs) and raw eggs, final cooking temperature at 145 F.
- 4th shelf = whole meats (pork and beef), final cooking temperature at 145 F.
- 5th shelf = comminuted ground meat and pooled eggs, final cooking temperature at 155 F.
- Bottom shelf = all poultry products, final cooking temperature at 165 F.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food. [P]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Observed that a wet mop was being stored in the lower basin of the mop bucket where it cannot air-dry. CORRECTED: PIC moved the mop to that the mop head was in the upper basket of the mop bucket, and any liquids can drain through the basket and be collected in the lower basin. Ensure that after use mops are placed so that they can air-dry without soiling their surroundings.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies. [C]

findings.title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
findings.comment: Employee was observed handling non ready to eat food from the prep cooler with their bare hands. CORRECTED- education about times to wash hands was provided. Ensure education about glove usage and  proper hand washing times are reviewed with new staff.
findings.citation_text: 3-301.11(C) Preventing Contamination from Hands. (C) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall minimize bare hand and arm contact with exposed FOOD that is not in a READY-TO-EAT form. [Pf]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment:
Sanitizer for food contact surfaces were observed to be outside of their recommended range in the following locations:
1) FIRST REPEAT The Quaternary ammonium sanitizer at the bar was observed to be at 100 ppm at the start of the inspection. CORRECTED- the sanitizer was remade and tested to be at 200 ppm of Quaternary ammonium. 
2) The kitchen’s Chlorine bleach sanitizer bucket was observed to be “bleaching out”- indicating too high of a concentration of bleach. CORRECTED- the bucket was diluted to 200 ppm.
Ensure that sanitizer is frequently tested using the facility’s test strips, and remade if not at the label-recommended concentration (200 to 400ppm for Quaternary ammonium and 50-200 ppm Cl for bleach).
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions. [P]

findings.title: Food properly labeled; original container.
findings.comment: Inspector observed an unlabeled white powder in the dry storage above the mop sink. CORRECTED- the item was identified as baking soda, and labeled accordingly. Ensure white powders (which may be easily mistaken for each other) are labeled once removed from their original container.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.12 Food Storage Containers, Identified with Common Name of Food. Except for containers holding FOOD that can be readily and unmistakably recognized such as dry pasta, working containers holding FOOD or FOOD ingredients that are removed from their original packages for use in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, such as cooking oils, flour, herbs, potato flakes, salt, spices, and sugar shall be identified with the common name of the FOOD. [C]

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored.
findings.comment: Inspector observed a wet wiping cloth on the kitchen prep counter. CORRECTED- the cloth was moved into the sanitizer bucket. Ensure that wet wiping cloths are always stored in sanitizing solutions between uses to prevent the growth and harborage of bacteria with high water activity. Dry wiping cloths may be used, as long as there are replaced at least every 4 hours.
findings.citation_text: 3-304.14(B) Wiping Cloths, Use Limitation. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be: (1) Held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution at a concentration specified under § 4-501.114; and (2) Laundered daily as specified under 4-802.11(D). [C]

Employees need to be informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with law to the PIC information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through food.

findings.title: Sewage and waste water properly disposed.

findings.citation_text: 5-402.13 Conveying Sewage. SEWAGE shall be conveyed to the point of disposal through an APPROVED sanitary SEWAGE system or other system, including use of SEWAGE transport vehicles, waste retention tanks, pumps, pipes, hoses, and connections that are constructed, maintained, and operated according to LAW.

findings.title: Food handler training
findings.comment:
An employee is observed to not have their food handler certificate. Ensure that all employees have their food handler certificate within 30 days of hire. 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

findings.comment:
3-501.16: Inspector observed corn and gravy cooled in the walk in that had been cooled on Wed (7/31) using an ice bath according to the manager. The internal temperature was observed to be 45F with a probe thermometer. The items were voluntarily discarded. The violation is considered corrected on site. Take care to cool food completely to 41F or below while the walk in cooler has an air temperature that will not facilitate cooling of the food. 

(A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less.

findings.comment:

The technician is here working on the unit.  The facility will have a re-inspection on 8/12/24 as the 8th is during the State Fair. 

EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures.

These items were thawing in the walk in unit.

(A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
Upon arrival, the inspector observed the hand sink blocked with a dirty dishes. The dishes were removed to the dish area and inspector washed hands. Never place items in a hand sink. Hand sinks shall be used for hand washing only. The violation is considered corrected on site. 

5-205.11: (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:
Inspector observed cardboard flats storing bagged food in the reach in portion of the pizza cooler. Use only smooth, nonabsorbent, easily cleanable containers to store food. Discontinue this practice by the next routine inspection.

4-101.11: (A) Materials used for FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES may not allow migration of deleterious substances shall be safe.
